title: Working with children: checks, supervision and reporting
audience: Tutors and education coaches (draft shell, no teaching content yet)
learningOutcomes: Explain why the check, supervision and reporting duties for a tutor depend on the jurisdiction and the role, and why this lesson does not state them for any state or territory.
Apply the supervision arrangement that the business owner and the expert reviewer have approved for the setting, and record it for each session.
Describe the steps to take when a child discloses harm or raises a concern, and identify who must be told.

instruction.heading: Checks before contact with children
instruction.body: Before a tutor works with a child, confirm whether a working-with-children check or an equivalent clearance is required for the role and the state or territory. Record the check type, the reference, the issue date and the expiry date, and set a reminder to renew before expiry. Do not begin unsupervised work with a child until the required check is confirmed. Where a check is not required, record the rule that was checked and the source it came from. The categories of check, and whether online or private-home tutoring falls under them, are UNCONFIRMED in this lesson.

instruction.heading: Supervision during sessions
instruction.body: Plan each session so that the learner is never alone with the tutor where the business rules forbid it. Typical arrangements are a parent or guardian in the home, a session in a room with a door that stays open or a window onto a common area, or an online session with a second adult present. Record who was present, the start and finish times, and where the session took place. Supervision ratios and the arrangement for each setting are set by the business owner and confirmed by the expert reviewer. Keep all contact with a learner inside the business's recorded channel. Do not exchange private messages or social media contact with a learner.

instruction.heading: Mandatory reporting
instruction.body: In some states and territories, certain adults must report a reasonable suspicion of child abuse or neglect to the child protection authority. Whether a tutor is one of those adults depends on the jurisdiction and the role, and this must be confirmed before the tutor starts work. Where a child is in immediate danger, call emergency services first. Where a concern is raised, write down the child's words as they were said, the date and time, and what was seen. Do not question the child beyond what is needed to understand what they said. Tell the business owner and follow the reporting route confirmed by the reviewer.

instruction.heading: Keeping the records
instruction.body: Keep attendance, supervision and check records in the business's recorded system, with access limited to people who need them. Do not keep copies of a child's personal documents unless the business rules and the applicable law allow it. The retention period for these records is UNCONFIRMED and must be set by the business owner with the reviewer.
